## 11. Implications for an Open-Source Gravimetric Powder Doser in Drug Discovery

For an inexpensive, open-source gravimetric powder doser targeting the milligram-to-gram range (as described in the user's context), the pharmaceutical drug discovery application space includes:

1. **Solubility screening**: Weighing solid APIs into vials for dissolution studies, as demonstrated with Quantos-based automated solubility platforms (shiri2021automatedsolubilityscreening pages 4-7).
2. **Stock solution preparation**: The upstream weighing step before dissolve-and-dispense workflows that feed acoustic or pin-tool liquid dispensing onto microplates (tu2026sticktothe pages 1-2, lisowski2026highthroughputsolidmicrosampling pages 1-3).
3. **Salt and polymorph screening**: Preparing diverse solid formulations at mg-scale for crystallization screens.
4. **Formulation development**: Dosing API and excipient powders for miniaturized tablet or capsule studies (abbas2025acceleratedmedicinesdevelopment pages 23-26).
5. **Catalyst/ligand dispensing**: Preparing solid reagents at mg-scale for HTE reaction screening, complementing ChemBead approaches for sub-milligram needs.

The key finding from the benchmarking literature is that at gram-scale targets (≥200 mg), even simple gravimetric feedback systems can achieve errors well below 1% for free-flowing powders (jiang2023autonomousbiomimeticsolid pages 8-10, jiang2023autonomousbiomimeticsolid pages 10-10). The challenge increases at lower targets (<20 mg) and with cohesive/difficult powders. An auger/vibratory feed with load-cell balance in the loop—as described in the user's system—is mechanistically similar to the Khinast micro-feeder concept and the SALSA Archimedes screw doser, suggesting achievable performance in the 1–20 g/h feed rate range with powder-dependent accuracy of approximately 4–20% RSD for challenging materials (fathollahi2020performanceevaluationof pages 11-12, hou2024developmentofa pages 57-61), improving substantially for free-flowing powders at larger doses.

| **SALSA 3D-printed Archimedes-screw doser** | Motor-driven 3D-printed screw in a Y-shaped PLA hopper; balance-in-the-loop endpoint control; interchangeable funnel geometry | Demonstrated from **≥0.3 g** | Standalone dosing error not reported; system-level solubility results were within about 20% of references | Not reported | Not reported | Particle-size distribution, viscosity, and flowability affect reproducibility; wider/shorter outlets were needed for fine, viscous salts (pqac-00000025, pqac-00000026) | PLA product-contact parts are inexpensive but difficult to validate for pharmaceutical cleaning, solvent compatibility, static control, and potent-compound containment | Very low-cost 3D-printed concept; exact bill of materials not reported |
| **Dissolve-and-dispense stock solution** | Prepare a known-concentration stock, then transfer it by pipette, pin tool, or acoustic liquid dispenser | Effective solid-equivalent dose can span ng–mg, determined by concentration and liquid volume | Liquid handling can be highly accurate, but overall error also includes initial weighing, volumetric preparation, evaporation, and concentration/solubility uncertainty | Instrument- and solution-dependent; not reported in the powder evidence | Usually much faster than direct powder dosing once stocks exist; acoustic transfer supports nL-scale downstream delivery | Avoids powder-flow problems but fails for insoluble, unstable, adsorptive, or precipitation-prone compounds; added solvent may perturb assays or chemistry (pqac-00000059, pqac-00000060) | Low cross-contamination with disposable tips or contactless acoustic transfer; stock preparation vessels still require cleaning, and DMSO/water uptake or evaporation must be controlled | Low if existing liquid handlers are used; acoustic dispensers are high-capital instruments |

info.query: Context: we are developing an inexpensive, open-source, gravimetric powder doser (auger / vibratory feed with a load-cell balance in the loop) for self-driving laboratories. It was designed for multi-powder dosing of metal powders for additive-manufacturing alloy discovery and targets the milligram-to-gram range; it is not intended for sub-milligram dosing. We want to know where it could be useful in drug discovery, in particular as the upstream 'weigh solid into a vial, then dissolve' step that precedes far smaller (nanoliter-to-picoliter) liquid dispensing onto microplates or lab-on-a-chip / organ-on-chip devices. Review the current technology for automated milligram- and gram-scale solid/powder dispensing used in pharmaceutical research and drug discovery: gravimetric dosing heads and platforms (Mettler Toledo Quantos and CHRONECT XPR, Chemspeed GDU-S SWILE / GDU-Pfd / FLEX / SWING / Crystal Powderdose, Unchained Labs (Freeslate) Junior and Big Kahuna, Zinsser Analytic, Labman, Symyx Powdernium, Sartorius, Hamilton, Brooks/Titian, Tecan), positive-displacement solid dispensers (e.g. SWILE), capsule micro-dosers for API-in-capsule (Capsugel Xcelodose, 3P Innovation Fill2Weigh), and alternative strategies (ChemBeads / coated-bead solid dispensing, dissolve-and-dispense stock-solution workarounds, vibratory / tapping / sieving micro-feeders, electrostatic or acoustic powder dosing). For each, report dose range, accuracy and %RSD (especially at 0.1-1 mg, 1-5 mg, 5-50 mg and gram targets), dispense time, dependence on powder properties (cohesive, electrostatic, hygroscopic, needle-shaped APIs; Hausner ratio, flow function), containment of potent compounds (OEB / OEL), cross-contamination and cleaning, and approximate cost. Include the multi-company benchmarking studies of automated powder dispensing in pharma high-throughput experimentation (e.g. Bahr et al. 2018 and 2020) and any newer 2021-2026 evaluations, plus open-source or low-cost academic powder dispensers built for self-driving labs. Provide a comparison table and full citations with DOIs.
